story:
In 2023 Anul Agarwal cloned the trending Suika Game in Unity in under two weeks: one week to get the gameplay right and one to polish. ChatGPT wrote all the C# gameplay code (dropper control, dropping, merging, win/lose, later new modes). He copy-pasted it into Unity, reported bugs back to the model, and added VFX and polish himself. The 11 kawaii fruit sprites were generated with DALL-E and cleaned up by hand.

Instead of chasing app stores, he licensed the game to web portals. By April 2024 he reported about $9.6k: GameDistribution ad share $1,500, a Coolmath Games license $2,500, Rainmaker Games $3,000, SuperSonic $300 and mobile ads $2,300. Coolmath lists its version as released on 16 January 2024. By May 2026 he reported $25k+ profit, 50–60M+ players across platforms, and #1 on Coolmath mobile, #3 on desktop and Game of the Year. He thinks moving faster on a mobile publisher could have added another $40–50k.

Tejas Kulkarni published 'Vibe Coding a Multi-player 3D FPS Game using AI' on 2025-03-10, the same week the vibe-coded game trend took off, crediting Anton Baumann for brainstorming, playtesting and help with the post. title: VibeSail
tagline: Multiplayer browser sailing sim from a dev with <2k followers that copied fly.pieter.com's ad model: $2.7k/mo in sponsors by day 8.

creator.name: Nicola Manzini
creator.background: solo indie hacker with under 2,000 X followers at launch (later cited as ~3,300)

summary: A minimalist, relaxing 3D sailing simulator in the browser where you see other players' boats live. There's free sailing, a tutorial, a daily race with a leaderboard, a world map and a 'High Sea' area, playable with keyboard, touch or gamepad on desktop or mobile. Businesses can sponsor islands, branded yachts and airborne banners.
highlights: Showed that fly.pieter.com's sponsor-ad model could be cloned within days by a near-unknown creator
$2,700/month in ad subscriptions eight days after launch
Live multiplayer boats in a zero-install browser game on desktop and mobile, with keyboard, touch or gamepad
Daily race, leaderboard, free sail and tutorial modes keep it replayable
Distribution hack: tagged and engaged the trend-setter (@levelsio) and got retweeted
story:
Nicola Manzini launched VibeSail in late February 2025, days after Pieter Levels' fly.pieter.com went viral, and copied the playbook. He built in public on X, tagged @levelsio in his update posts (Levels retweeted him several times), and sold ad space on in-game islands. With fewer than 2,000 followers he reported $2,700 in monthly ad subscriptions when the game was eight days old (6 March 2025). Secondary listings later put it at ~$8k MRR (~$96k ARR) by April 2025, one says 'almost $10,000', and Starter Story says it grew after an Elon Musk endorsement (single source).

Indie Hackers featured Manzini in 'How 5 vibe-coded AI games went viral despite their creators having tiny audiences' as a counterexample to the 'it only worked because of Levels' audience' argument. The game is still live and has added daily races and leaderboards.

vibeCoding.aiCodeShare: unknown (one secondary listing claims ~85% AI-generated; unverified)
vibeCoding.buildTime: unknown; launched within days of fly.pieter.com and kept being updated in public
workflow: Built in public on X with frequent update posts tagging @levelsio
Copied fly.pieter.com's monetization: sponsored islands, branded yachts, airborne banners

Starter Story's auto-compiled tool list includes Cursor, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, bolt.new, Three.js, Supabase, Netlify and Cloudflare. It warns the list may be misattributed, so treat the tools as unverified

art.notes: Graphics are 'powered by Three.js'. Sources don't say whether the boats and islands are code-generated or come from models or packs.

tech.notes: Real-time multiplayer that connects players automatically. Starter Story lists Netlify, Supabase, Cloudflare, Google Analytics and Zapier, but that list was auto-compiled and is unverified.

traction.monetization: Free to play, funded by in-game advertising subscriptions (sponsored islands, branded yachts, airborne banners), listed at $100/month per slot by aiapps.com and Starter Story.
traction.notes: Revenue numbers come from the creator's posts as relayed by newsletters and listings. Player counts are undisclosed ('thousands of players').

reception: Indie Hackers held it up as virality without an audience, and @levelsio amplified it. There's little independent press or criticism.
lessons: Small creators can borrow distribution by tagging and engaging the big account whose trend they're riding
A proven monetization template (in-world sponsor slots) can be copied in days, but it depends on a hype window
Revenue claims for these games come from creator tweets and are rarely verifiable

title: Mine8
tagline: The most-played game on Verse8's prompt-to-game platform: a timed mining upgrade loop with 3M+ plays and in-platform purchases.

creator.name: Snack Games
creator.background: creator/studio publishing on Verse8; no further details disclosed

summary: A stage-based mining game: you swing a pickaxe at rock formations on a dirt field and collect a target number of ores before the timer runs out. Gold from each stage buys better pickaxes (trading off swing speed, damage and durability) and upgrades four passive and four active skills like Auto Lightning and Splash Damage. Mystery boxes appear on the terrain, and auto-mining keeps earning ores while you're offline.
highlights: Most-played game on a prompt-to-game platform: 3M+ plays and 1,100 likes (April 2026)
A complete F2P meta-loop built on an AI platform: pickaxe shop with stat trade-offs, 4 passive and 4 active upgradeable skills, mystery boxes, and an option to double rewards
Monetized through Verse8's VX currency: 249 VX for ad-free plus double rewards, Gold/Special Box packs, and premium offline auto-mining for up to 24h
Difficulty ramps after stage 100, and some players pass stage 200 in a single session
story: Mine8 was made by Snack Games on Verse8, an AI-native platform where games are generated from natural-language prompts by the Agent8 agent on Verse8's own WebGL engine. Planetarium Labs launched Verse8 publicly on 15 July 2025, developed with Lineage and ArcheAge creator Jake Song. In March 2026 Odaily called Mine8 the platform's most popular mini-game, and Phaser's news site reported 3M+ plays and 1,100 likes as of April 2026, making it the most-played game on Verse8. Some players clear 200+ stages in one session, and the top requests are cross-device sync and the ability to revisit earlier stages for materials that later become unavailable.

vibeCoding.aiCodeShare: unknown (the platform generates game code from prompts)
vibeCoding.buildTime: unknown
workflow: Verse8's Agent8 turns prompts into game code on a built-in WebGL engine with genre templates (RPG, platformer, idle, FPS) and suggests improvements as you go
Users choose which LLM to use; the platform also auto-adapts 2D assets, rigs and optimizes 3D models, and connects gen-AI tools for assets and audio (including via MCP)
Bug loop (per Google Cloud's case study): the platform runs the game in a sandbox, captures error logs and feeds them back to the LLM
'Spin' lets anyone fork a published game in one click and remix it

art.notes: Verse8 offers built-in AI asset generation, but Mine8's art provenance isn't documented.

tech.notes: Runs on Verse8's proprietary browser WebGL engine (real-time 3D and multiplayer capable). Mine8's own architecture isn't documented, and its fetched page sat behind a security check.

traction.monetization: Ads plus a VX-currency shop (ad-free plus double rewards for 249 VX, Gold/Special Box packs, premium offline auto-mining). Verse8 is building creator reward programs (a $10,000 Creator Partner pool), but payout terms aren't public.
traction.notes: Play counts are platform-reported and unaudited, and the creator, build time and revenue are undisclosed.

reception: Little independent coverage: mostly Phaser's news roundup and crypto-adjacent outlets (Odaily, HTX) writing about Verse8. Player feedback centres on cross-device progress sync and revisiting earlier stages.
lessons: On prompt-to-game platforms, the hit is a simple, sticky casual loop with F2P monetization, not an ambitious world
Platform-hosted play counts are reported by the platform itself and can't be independently checked
Players expect persistence features like cross-device save sync even from AI-made mini-games

title: Vibeware
tagline: WarioWare for internet chores: play a scraping bot racing through microgames like typing 4242 into Stripe. 2025 Vibe Jam silver.

creator.name: Matt Gordon
creator.background: Maker of viral novelty apps (his site cites Bufferi.ng, TwikTwok, MpTr.ee); not primarily a game dev

summary: A WarioWare-style string of rapid microgames built on everyday phone and web chores, like typing 4242 into a Stripe checkout, skipping ads and closing pop-ups. You play a scraping bot. It was mobile-first, had a deliberately 'very annoying' soundtrack, and let players add their own microgames using instructions meant to be pasted into an LLM.
highlights: Turns muscle-memory internet chores (Stripe test cards, ad skips, pop-ups) into microgames
Built with just React and web APIs, with no game engine
Players could extend it: it shipped instructions to paste into an LLM to generate new microgames
Mobile-first design
Grew into an iOS follow-up, Training Data – AI Microgames
story: Matt Gordon submitted Vibeware to the 2025 Vibe Coding Game Jam on April 1, 2025 and took Silver ($5,000). He later wrote that 'people loved the game.' After sitting on the idea for about a year, he expanded it into 'Training Data – AI Microgames,' an iOS game where you play an AI gathering training data through 'unhinged microgames' that use the camera and other sensors. The original web version at vibeware.vercel.app now shows a 'working on something new' teaser, so the jam game is no longer playable.
